runtimeFlags: sycl backend, -ngl 99 -fa 1 -ncmoe 8 -p 512 -n 256 -r 5, single request. Expert tensors of the first 8 of 48 layers are held in system RAM; the model does not fit in 32GB of VRAM.
notes: Stock upstream ggml-org/llama.cpp b11026 (b49650adb), clean tree, sycl backend. Weights ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF, Q2_0 (GSQ-RCO non-uniform, 61.9GiB) - the smallest full-weight GGUF of this model that exists. 176.9B parameters, roughly 3B active per token. Partial CPU offload via -ncmoe 8: expert tensors of 8 of 48 layers sit in system RAM, 24.2GiB of weights on the card. 8 is both the optimum and the floor; -ncmoe 4 aborts out of VRAM. decodeTps and promptTps are llama-bench tg256/pp512 from a short prompt, 5 runs, one at a time - i.e. at negligible context depth, matching the other results here. LIVE SERVING, NOT A BENCHMARK, same machine and weights at -ncmoe 16: a 41,415-token prompt with a cold cache took 157.2s to first token (263.4 tok/s prefill), then generated at 19.4 tok/s. A 413-token prompt against a warm cache: 141.9 tok/s prefill, 19.3 tok/s decode. Sustained decode measured 19.5-21.7 tok/s across 22k-41k tokens of context. Most of the gap from the 28.15 figure is context depth, not offload: a tg256 sweep at depth 0 gives 28.13 at -ncmoe 8 versus 27.13 at -ncmoe 16, about 1 tok/s. Prefill holds up with length where decode does not - 263 tok/s at 41k tokens.
